institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study in Paris, get better at French and get the experience of going on exhchange

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Everything about it was really good, only some small burdens at Sciences Po and some courses can be commented on.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite difficult. They had an intro-day, but we did not get any information about finding our way around. But I had received adresses for my courses, so they were okay to find.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an intro-course, which I did not participate in as it cost 250 Euro. An intro-day was also available.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Used facebook groups and contacts who had been in Paris previously.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's the only real possibility at Sciences Po. But a big part of the experience of living abroad.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Don't know, I found my own. But it took some patience.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: This is the worst part. You have to be ready to access a website at a specific time, and when it opens, everything is in French. You have to have found your courses beforehand and know their names and codes, as almost all subjects are completely full after 3-5 minutes. Once a course is full, there is not really a way to get it, unless you contact the administration. You have to try and get the classes that are mandatory first, then find electives after. All in all, it is a very stressfull process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the subjects I needed.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare a list of courses, where you know the course names and codes. And be ready on time, that way you'll probably get what you need

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were not that difficult. They are graded differently than in Copenhagen, as there are multiple components, such as participation, presentations and papers.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More participation from students and generally smaller classes. Only had one course with a lecture (forelæsning). Teachers less pedagogical

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Comparative politics
European Foreign and Security Policies
The Euro, Migration and Climate Change: European Challenges and Opportunities
Green Parties and their Electorate in Europe. 
Arab Monarchies of the Persian Gulf: New MiddleEastern Powers

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Arab Monarchies of the Persian Gulf: New MiddleEastern Powers - great teacher and really interesting. His name is Kevin Gefaïti, find something he is teaching. 
The Euro, Migration and Climate Change: European Challenges and Opportunities - Very clear teacher, but has his own style.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Paris is expensive in some areas, but in other areas really cheap and nice. So it's hard to say, but it was more or less as I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sorts of sports, same sign-up procedure as for courses. Less stressfull

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did yoga, which was a great experience

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Get the Erasmus-Interrail pass - makes transport to and from the city easy and allows for trips around Europe. Go to sports events and other stuff, always something going on in Paris.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy. Nice city to live in!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find it challenging, but I speak French, which I think helps a bit.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Slower pace, the cafes, how much happens around the city, the culture and the language. Overall super good experience to be there

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be ready to sign up to classes!
The courses may seem difficult, and take some time, but they are quite generous with grades and you will pass the courses, so don't stress. Attendance is annoying
Give yourself time to enjoy Paris also

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is attendance for courses at Sciences Po - you can only miss two lectures pr. course during the semester.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed the social parts, linguistic development and some of my courses, which were really interesting and more niche than at KU

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't know

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
